📊 DAILY METALS PULSE — SEPTEMBER 3

The metals complex turned decisively green as markets backed away from their most hawkish Fed expectations.

The response:

🥈 Silver +2.8% to ~$67.13

SILVER: Once again outperforming gold when the monetary tide turns. Back above $67, silver retains two engines: precious-metal demand and relentless industrial consumption.

COPPER: Holding close to record territory despite concerns about China’s property sector. Mine-supply constraints, distorted global inventories and growing power-grid, EV and AI demand continue to support the long-term scarcity thesis.

URANIUM: No dramatic daily move, but holding near six-month highs is itself significant. Kazatomprom’s sulphuric-acid constraints remain unresolved, while the West still lacks enough secure conversion and enrichment capacity to replace Russian supply comfortably.

Tomorrow’s US payroll report is the next major test. A soft number could drive yields and the dollar lower again; a strong number would likely create volatility.

Four different metals, four different markets, but one underlying message:

The world needs more monetary protection, electricity, infrastructure and secure energy than the existing supply system is prepared to provide.

MYRIAD IS DRILLING INTO A HISTORICAL 655 MILLION POUND URANIUM ENDOWMENT

That is the scale of the opportunity at Copper Mountain, and Myriad Uranium is now generating the modern data needed to determine how much of it can ultimately be converted into a compliant resource.

A detailed 1982 study by Bendix Engineering for the U.S. Department of Energy estimated a potential uranium endowment of:

⚛️ Approximately 245 Mlbs eU₃O₈ within the core Control Area
⚛️ Approximately 655 Mlbs eU₃O₈ across the broader Assessment Area
Both estimates extended only to a depth of 600 feet.

These figures are historical and conceptual, not current mineral resources, but they were based on extensive technical work and access to Union Pacific’s enormous dataset. Around 2,000 boreholes were drilled historically at Copper Mountain, with Union Pacific investing an estimated C$125 million in today’s money.

Phase II drilling is now advancing quickly:

🔹 Lucky Cliff: initial results released and assays pending
🔹 Gem: drilling completed and results ahead
🔹 Hesitation: drill team now on site

At Lucky Cliff, all four holes encountered multiple intervals of near-surface uranium mineralization. Myriad reported 50 intervals above 100 ppm eU₃O₈, including 19.96 metres at 269 ppm from only 18 metres and a peak grade of 1,336 ppm.
Crucially, Lucky Cliff lies outside the entire Bendix Assessment Area.
In other words, Myriad has found broad mineralization beyond even the area associated with the historical 655 Mlb endowment estimate.

Drilling has also been completed at Gem, historically estimated to contain 1.44 Mlbs at approximately 0.023% eU₃O₈.

The drill team has now moved to Hesitation, which carries a historical estimate of 2.20 Mlbs at approximately 0.025%.

The investment case is therefore much larger than the initial historical estimate of 26.63 Mlbs.

Myriad is testing a district where historical work suggested hundreds of millions of pounds, and its first Phase II target has already confirmed mineralization beyond the boundaries of that historical assessment.

If modern drilling continues to validate the old geological model, Copper Mountain could emerge as one of the largest undeveloped uranium systems in the United States.

The potential scale is already documented.

Now Myriad is drilling to prove it.

Disclosure: Paid partnership with Myriad Uranium. Please do your own research.

Another reason why semis are hard (and more broadly, equities), and no longer the hot ball of money is because things are no longer linear, easy to understand

Longing most "global trends" generate the most returns - in 2021, you long crypto (it was the biggest thing); 2023, financials, 2025, semis

These homerun trades often focus on one core theme: Demand is increasing, this benefits. And most homerun trades, if you look in the past 5 years, have all come from this simple seed

The moment a thematic starts becoming more complex, it fails. Investors become uncertain if what they're holding is what will be needed. And that's where AI is right now.

Take a look at AVGO's earnings. AVGO reported extraordinary numbers - F3Q revenue +85.5% YoY - and introduced FY27/FY28 AI revenue targets of $115B/$230B. FY28 potentially supports >$30 EPS. 

But AVGO sold off because FY27 was below buyside expectations of ~$130–150B and the growth increasingly depends on OpenAI + Anthropic. Around 15GW of the roughly 20GW FY28 deployment discussed comes from those two customers. 

On the other hand, software, which was thought to be left for dead, is incredibly strong. SNOW is up 16% - Product growth accelerated sharply, about half the acceleration came from AI products, CoCo adoption reached ~63%, cRPO accelerated, and margins are holding up better than expected. 

All of a sudden, software may be the enterprise control plane for AI agents? No one knows. And so the AI trade is basically unwinding on itself, because its so hard to forecast the future

Markets are ever-evolving, and so, IMO, it's more worthwhile to figure out where the puck will be 6 months from now
